column1: # The pgvector statements of the postgresql language (fork issue #11), with expected answers that come from the definitions of the
# operators and not from a server: the official postgres:18 image of the parity run has no pgvector, and the extension is not added
# to it. Every case is flagged doc. The engine tests read this file (PgVectorDocCorpusTest); the parity harness does not.
# Columns, separated by one TAB: id, order, tol, status, statement, expected. The cells are those of answers.tsv (see its header):
# order is ordered or multiset, tol is a floating point tolerance, statement escapes backslash, tab and line feed, expected is
# {"columns":[labels],"types":[type names],"rows":[[cells]]} or {"error":"SQLSTATE"}.
# status: doc = the expected cells were worked out by hand from the text named below. A case that fails is a difference between the
# engine and the definition, to be settled by reading pgvector 0.8 (its source, or a server that has it), never by editing the cell.
# Sources of the cells:
#   README: pgvector README, section "Querying" (Supported distance functions are <-> L2 distance, <#> (negative) inner product,
#   <=> cosine distance), section "Distances" (for cosine similarity, use 1 - cosine distance), section "Getting Started" (the
#   vectors [1,2,3] and [4,5,6]), and section "Reference", "Vector Type" (finite elements, up to 16,000 dimensions).
#   #11: the acceptance list of fork issue #11 (the fixture vec-small: a [1,0,0], b [0,1,0], c [2,2,0], d [-1,0,0], the query vector
#   [1,0,0], the three ORDER BY results and the table of distances). Its values are the definitions applied by hand: sqrt(2),
#   source: the error cases (22000 for vectors of different dimensions, 22P02 for text that is not a vector) are not in the README:
#   they are the SQLSTATE of pgvector's CheckDims and vector_in in its vector.c.
# data: the vec-small fixture, VecSmallFixture in the engine tests, without an index. The same statements with an LSM_VECTOR index of
# the matching metric are asserted in VectorSearchPlanTest.
id
doc-l2-order
column5: SELECT iid FROM item ORDER BY embedding <-> '[1,0,0]' LIMIT 3

column1: doc-cosine-order
column5: SELECT iid FROM item ORDER BY embedding <=> '[1,0,0]' LIMIT 3

column1: doc-inner-product-order
column5: SELECT iid FROM item ORDER BY embedding <#> '[1,0,0]' LIMIT 3

column1: doc-distances
column5: SELECT iid, embedding <-> '[1,0,0]' AS l2, embedding <=> '[1,0,0]' AS cosine, embedding <#> '[1,0,0]' AS ip FROM item ORDER BY iid

column1: doc-cosine-similarity
column5: SELECT iid, 1 - (embedding <=> '[1,0,0]') AS cosine_similarity FROM item ORDER BY iid
